# find_super_connectors { #dyf.find_super_connectors }

```python
find_super_connectors(
    embeddings,
    global_num_bits=None,
    facet_num_bits=None,
    dense_percentile=75,
    global_threshold_percentile=50,
    local_threshold_percentile=50,
    min_bucket_size=20,
    seed=42,
    bridge_percentile=10,
)
```

Find super connectors: points with high centrality in both global and local
bridge networks.

Super connectors are ideal RAG anchor points because they:
- Bridge across major semantic regions (high global centrality)
- Connect facets within dense clusters (high local centrality)
- Provide 10x better coverage efficiency than random anchors

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                        | Type                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Default    |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| embeddings                  | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Normalized embeddings (n_points, dim)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | _required_ |
| global_num_bits             | [int](`int`) \| None                     | LSH bits for global bucketing. ``None`` (default) derives it from the corpus size via :func:`_derive_num_bits`, which is required for the dense-bucket gate to open at all below ~8k points — the previous fixed default of 12 returned zero super connectors on every smaller corpus.                                                                            | `None`     |
| facet_num_bits              | [int](`int`) \| None                     | LSH bits for facet bucketing within a dense bucket. ``None`` (default) uses two bits below the global resolution.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `None`     |
| dense_percentile            | [float](`float`)                         | Percentile threshold for dense buckets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `75`       |
| global_threshold_percentile | [float](`float`)                         | Percentile for "high" global centrality                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `50`       |
| local_threshold_percentile  | [float](`float`)                         | Percentile for "high" local centrality                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `50`       |
| min_bucket_size             | [int](`int`)                             | Minimum bucket size for faceting                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `20`       |
| seed                        | [int](`int`)                             | Random seed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `42`       |
| bridge_percentile           | [float](`float`)                         | Bridges are the lowest-centroid-similarity points; this is the percentile of *this corpus's* similarity distribution used as the cut. Relative by design — `analyze_bridges`'s absolute 0.5 default returns zero bridges on unit-norm text embeddings (0.0% fall below it) and floods on isotropic data (92.3% below), so an absolute constant cannot serve both. | `10`       |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                   | Description                                           |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [SuperConnectorResult](`dyf.rag.SuperConnectorResult`) | SuperConnectorResult with indices and centrality data |
